hints.title: Single Row Character Subset
hints.text: A word can be typed using letters from one keyboard row only if all its characters belong to that same row.

hints.title: Row Set Membership Invariant
hints.text: Representing the three keyboard rows as character sets permits checking whether the characters of a word form a subset of any row.

hints.title: Row Subset Filter Procedure
hints.text: Define three collections for the keyboard rows. For each word, convert its letters to lowercase. If all letters are contained within row one, row two, or row three, add the original word to the output list. Return the list.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N * L) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking letter rows with nested linear searches over strings introduces redundant character scans.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant lookup tables verify row membership in O(L) time per word, taking O(N * L) total time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle case insensitivity cleanly and preserve the original capitalization in the output.
